title: Trainstorm Audience Model — segment record
description: The Audience Agent's write schema (agents-roster: 'the ethnographer — knows the people; never touches the content'). One record per audience SEGMENT: the design-time learner/audience model the unification map calls Band B-sub (ADRA S6.1–S6.6 + S7 — affective, cadence, empathy, meaning, inhibitor, motivator, composite indices), keyed to segments, never to persons. This is the sibling graph: it lives beside the content graph (a project's audience/<segment_id>.json, next to voice/ and locales/) and joins it ONLY through objective_ids (mastery, factor targeting) and, downstream, through element_id when a planner binds direction per segment. It is also the LRE Stage-1 'synthetic learner': a segment record enacted as a persona IS the learner the planner plans for (see architecture/lre-stage1-synthetic-learner.md). The same shape is reserved for Stage 2's live learner record (kind=learner) so that the planner cannot tell synthetic from live — but that record is written by the Responsive Engine under separate learner-data governance and MUST NOT appear in a content project store; the gate rejects it there. PII-BLIND BY CONSTRUCTION: no name, identifier, contact, or free text about a person; every psychological value is a governed vocabulary id plus a strength and a basis (why we believe it — a reviewable reason, never a confidence score), so a reason trace can cite it. NO SILENT LYING: this record holds only what a population can hold before any course exists. The trajectory variables (clarity, agreement, intent_to_act, load) are deliberately absent — they arise during an encounter and belong to the scene's learning contract, not to the audience.

record_id.description: Stable opaque id of this record. seg_… for a segment record (Audience Agent, design time). lrn_… is RESERVED for the Responsive Engine's live learner record (Stage 2, separate governance) and is not legal in a content project store.

kind.description: segment = design-time population record; the Stage-1 synthetic learner. learner = Stage-2 live record (reserved; not written by any agent yet). Must agree with the record_id prefix.

segment_id.description: The audience segment this record describes. The design-time join: elements target it via audience.segment_scope[]; a direction planner keys per-segment bindings by it.

as_of.description: When this record was true. Segment: the analysis/authoring time. Learner (reserved): the last evidence update.

standing.description: Survey-depth facts about the population's position (ADRA S1 / Audience Analysis): role, tier, experience, what they already know. The Audience Agent writes this on project intake, before any deep pass.

role.description: Role id (registry/roles.registry.json where one applies) — a population's role, never a person's title.

tier.description: Risk/responsibility tier id (e.g. an RBT tier).

mastery.description: Estimated mastery per objective, as priors for the population. Keyed by obj_ ids from ontology/objectives.json — the audience model joins content through OBJECTIVES, not elements, so a segment record survives re-export and is reusable across courses.

prior_exposure.description: Courses/topics this population has typically completed, as ids — never free text.

disposition.description: The deep pass — B-sub proper. What the psykido skills produce when the Designer flags a persuasive nature (unification-map §5): inhibitors, objections, aligners/motivators, identity threats, belief gaps, meaning anchors, rationalization patterns, dominant affect. Every factor is a governed id from vocab/disposition.enum.json with a strength, a basis, and a risk_of_overuse — the roster's one hard ethical rule, carried on the thing it protects. These are what the psychological primitives reason FROM; the primitives themselves are never stored here or in content.

inhibitors.description: What blocks uptake or action (inh_). Inhibitor Vaccination (S6.5) targets these.

objections.description: Counter-arguments the population is likely to hold (obj_x_ — NOT obj_, which is reserved for objectives).

aligners.description: Values/goals the content can align with (aln_). Motivation Reinforcer (S6.6) targets these.

identity_threats.description: Ways the content could read as an attack on who the learner is (thr_). Empathy Tuning (S6.4).

belief_gaps.description: Misconceptions or missing mental models at population level (gap_). Meaning Maker (S6.3). Item-level misconception_predictions live on knowledge_check primitives in the CONTENT graph — not here.

meaning_anchors.description: What makes this matter to them (mng_). Meaning Maker (S6.3).

rationalization_patterns.description: Characteristic ways the population explains away the behavior being taught (rat_). ADRA's rationalization_pattern, segment-level.

affective_pattern.description: Dominant emotional stance toward the subject, governed id (aff_). Affective Patterns (S6.1).

baselines.description: B-sub S7 — the composite indices, as population BASELINES the Audience Agent seeds: dispositions a population can plausibly hold before any course exists. Static in Stage 1; no update machinery exists or may exist for them here. EXACTLY FOUR, on purpose (design beat 2026-09-01, 'split it is'): the other four candidates — clarity, agreement, intent_to_act, load — are trajectories that arise during an encounter and are the TARGET of a scene, not a property of an audience. They belong to the scene's learning contract (Designer's facet; capability_horizon/learner-response-intelligence, 'moment-level learning contract') and to evidence flags in Stage 1.5. Writing them here would be a schema asserting a state that does not yet exist.

self_efficacy.description: Does this population believe it can do what is asked?

risk_sensitivity.description: How much do consequences weigh on them? (High: consequences carry themselves; don't amplify.)

identity_safety.description: Do they feel their competence/identity is safe in this subject? (Low: anchor before asserting.)

cadence.description: Engagement Cadence (S6.2) — how this population takes in material. Read directly by a direction planner for chunking and pacing.

chunk_tolerance.description: How much per beat before attention drops.

interaction_appetite.description: How often the population wants to DO rather than receive.

governance.description: Provenance of this record. Same shape family as element.governance so tooling can reuse. owner is the Audience Agent for segment records.

owner.description: Accountable owner id — audience_agent for segment records.

generated_by.description: Agent/skill-chain id + version that produced this record, e.g. audience_agent.psykido.v1.

source_hash.description: Hash of the audience analysis this record was distilled from. Changed hash ⇒ record stale ⇒ any per-segment direction bindings stale.

derived_from.description: Ids of the analysis artifacts / dossier this record was distilled from.

reviewer_notes.description: Reviewer commentary on the RECORD as an artifact — never about a real person.

ext.description: Sanctioned extension point, as in element.schema. Experimental audience fields accrete here; promote once stable.

basis.description: Why we believe this value — a short, consistent, human-reviewable reason token of the form <source>:<ref>, never a confidence number and never prose (design decision 2026-08: 'a reason statement is better than a value'). Segment: the analysis that asserted it. Learner (reserved): an evidence ref.

risk_of_overuse.description: ADRA S6.6 — the only harm model in any layer, promoted to a GATE (unification-map §2). Asks whether targeting this factor could harm the person it is aimed at: manipulation, shame, identity injury, learned helplessness. A planner MUST read it: high ⇒ this factor may be acknowledged but never amplified or repeated; moderate ⇒ once per course; low ⇒ no constraint. A factor without it cannot be targeted.

id.description: Governed id from vocab/disposition.enum.json. Free text is NOT allowed — an ungoverned factor cannot appear in a reason trace, and the gate rejects ids the vocabulary does not define.

objective_ids.description: Optional: the objectives this factor bears on most (segment × objective entries, per the roster), so a planner can localize its response.
